## Gates

- `just setup` prepares managed Python storage, installs both frozen lockfiles,
  builds TypeScript and restores Dropbox marks where required; errors fail setup.
- Focused work: `just test-one python tests/test_paths.py` or
  `just test-one ts tests/paths.test.ts`. Selectors are relative to the named
  package; a language and selector are required and argv is forwarded intact.
- `just test-fast` selects affected tests (pytest-testmon and Vitest changed).
  `just test` requests both full suites; `just test-full` forces them explicitly.
- `just check` composes mandatory `just check-hygiene` (ops-check, ops-docs and
  tasks check) with broad `just check-code` (Ruff, Pyright, tsc and Biome).
  `just gate` composes check and test. Run recipes from anywhere in the tree.
- Checkout-local `.tt.toml`, validated by `tools/tt`, governs broad execution.
  The committed policy disables automatic broad work. Missing policy means enabled.
  Policy skips have null outcomes, never passing
  suites. Focused/setup/hygiene routes are protected. Deliberate broad checks use
  `TT_FORCE=1`; hosted broad verification requires that explicit setting.
- Every executed check goes through `tools/tt`; do not call pytest, npm test,
  Ruff, Pyright, tsc or Biome directly. Composing aliases add no timer.
- Git hooks retain hygiene and request broad children separately. Hook timing now
  measures hygiene only; the old hook and check timing series do not continue.
  Fresh clones install hooks with `git config core.hooksPath .githooks`.
- CI keeps Python 3.11/3.13 and Node 20/24, sets `TT_FORCE=1` explicitly and
  retains per-job JUnit/module inventory artifacts for 30 days. Its validated
  configuration covers branch pushes and fork PRs, with reusable Release calls.
  Origin coverage is declared for `refs/heads/*` and Release's `refs/tags/v*`.
  Branch CI and a manual Release run validated the callable path; actual tag
  execution remains untested. Results are in the activation packet.
- Before removing a worktree, run `tt-report` in ops to harvest fallback timings.
- See `docs/test-execution-policy.md` for setup location handling, force commands,
  coverage, activation evidence and rollback limits.

## Layout

- `python/`, `ts/` — the two packages; `fixtures/` — the shared conformance oracles.
- `docs/STANDARD.md` — the authority; `docs/designs/`, `docs/plans/` — dated records,
  rationale only.

## Rules

- Authority order: `docs/STANDARD.md`, then the code and its tests, then the dated
  records. When anything disagrees with the standard, it wins, or it has a bug: fix it
  in the same change. Do not execute old plans or treat their snippets as current.
- Layering is enforced: `nodes.core` imports nothing above it and names zero knowledge
  kinds; domain kinds live downstream, registered onto the kernel's `Registry`.
- Decide the parity tier before any feature (`docs/STANDARD.md` §1): tier 1 (format,
  identity, mutation semantics) and tier 2 (derived-index behavior, finding codes) land
  in both languages with the standard and the `fixtures/` oracles in the same change;
  tier 3 (per-language convenience) may be one language with no standard change.
- Wrap Pydantic/Zod errors into the kernel error hierarchy; they never escape public
  APIs. Kinds are name + facets + invariants, never subclasses.
- Vocabulary: a **kind** composes facets and invariants under a name and may adopt one
  registered **shape** (how members hang together; `set`, `list`, `dict`, `graph`,
  `dag`, `tree` ship built in, and a registry accepts others); a **facet** is a named,
  typed payload (the domain mix-in); a **structure** is a node whose kind adopts a
  shape. "Subclass" and "inherits" never describe a kind. The README's "The model"
  subsection is the reader's version of this list.
- Boundary: an external identifier (a CURIE, a DOI, a vocabulary term) is an opaque
  string inside a facet. The kernel never resolves, fetches or interprets one; a
  resolver is a downstream concern, and no kernel code path may branch on its content.
